page: Amazon Web Services mac-m4.metal is a bare-metal macOS server instance powered by an Apple M4 silicon processor. The system features 10 physical cores and 10 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.5 GHz on the arm64_mac architecture, with a dedicated single-threaded core allocation without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of unified system memory, yielding 2.4 GB of RAM per dedicated physical core.

Storage and connectivity are integrated directly into the bare-metal package. The instance includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for high-speed file operations and compiler caching, paired with a baseline network bandwidth capacity of 10 Gbps. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not provide discrete GPU acceleration, relying entirely on the native Apple system-on-chip hardware.

Designed specifically for the Apple ecosystem, the mac-m4.metal instance provides dedicated hardware access without hypervisor overhead. This configuration is directly targeted at continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, native macOS and iOS application compilation, Xcode automated test suites, and general-purpose arm64 software development.
description: Amazon Web Services mac-m4.metal is a dedicated bare-metal macOS server powered by a 10-core Apple M4 processor built on the arm64_mac architecture. Operating at 3.5 GHz across 10 physical cores without hyperthreading, the instance provides 24.0 GB of system memory at an allocation ratio of 2.4 GB per core. It integrates 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and offers a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no discrete GPU hardware. The non-virtualized bare-metal profile delivers predictable execution speeds for Apple platform workloads, removing hypervisor resource contention. This architecture is engineered primarily for macOS and iOS build pipelines, automated Xcode integration testing, and native arm64 code compilation.
